prompt: Original educational conceptual illustration, landscape 3:2. Warm ivory paper, sophisticated hand-painted gouache/watercolour, confident fine brown outlines, navy lettering, restrained teal, coral and amber. Editorial science illustration with spacious composition and large legible labels. The explanatory structure must carry the meaning visually: molecules, objects, geometry or flow; never paragraphs in boxes. No organs, regional anatomy, teeth or joint cutaways, tissue layers, invented histology, diagnostic photographs, radiographs or patient data. All symbols are explicitly conceptual. Footer: 'Conceptual teaching model • Not to scale'. Title 'More obstruction diverts more flow', subtitle 'Flow principle in tetralogy'. Two side-by-side abstract Y-shaped WATER-CHANNEL STYLE diagrams carved in wood, not vascular anatomy. Each has ONE input from the left that splits into an upper route labelled 'Toward lungs' and a lower route labelled 'Bypass to body'. Left heading 'Less obstruction': upper route has a fairly open small mechanical gate and a broad teal flow arrow; lower route a thinner navy arrow. Right heading 'Greater obstruction': same upper-route gate almost closed, tiny teal arrow still passing toward lungs; lower-route navy bypass arrow is clearly much broader than on the left. No branch rejoins, no extra inlets. Only relative arrow widths, no numbers. Takeaway 'Less lung flow; more bypass'. Footer 'Flow analogy, not a heart map'. No heart, organs, named vessels, chambers, valves or patients.

clinicalSources.title: Sydney Children’s Hospitals Network: Tetralogy of Fallot and hypercyanotic spells

teaching.question: Why can severe outflow obstruction cause marked cyanosis early in tetralogy of Fallot?
teaching.answer: It limits flow toward the lungs and promotes more right-to-left bypass to the systemic circulation, reducing oxygenation.

title: More obstruction diverts more flow
caption: In tetralogy of Fallot, greater right-ventricular outflow obstruction reduces flow toward the lungs and promotes right-to-left bypass, worsening cyanosis. This abstract split shows the flow principle only.
alt: Two identical forked channels compare a relatively open lung route with a narrowed lung route and larger bypass arrow to the body.

review.notes: Pixel check: each side has one input splitting into exactly two abstract outputs. Greater obstruction nearly closes only the toward-lungs gate, narrows that arrow and enlarges bypass-to-body flow. Both directions are downstream and labels remain matched; explicit flow-analogy caption avoids a cardiac anatomy claim.
